title: Robust or Suggestible? Exploring Non-Clinical Induction in LLM Drug-Safety Decisions
benchmark_measurement: Bias in Large Language Model (LLM) predictions for medical adverse events, specifically measuring how prediction accuracy changes when a patient is assigned a religious identity (Jewish, Christian, Atheist, or generically 'Religious').
findings: LLMs exhibited systematic disparities in prediction accuracy based on religious personas. ChatGPT-4o underperformed for religious personas and frequently referenced religious identity in its reasoning (over 50% of cases for the 'Religious' persona). Bio-Medical-Llama-3-8B showed significant accuracy drops for the 'Religious' persona under the 'Patient' user role. Removing cases where religious identity was explicitly mentioned in the model's reasoning led to notable accuracy gains, indicating that the bias is embedded in the model's behavior and not just its explicit justifications.
